routes.summary: Complete a task or subtask.
routes.help:
Complete a task or subtask.

Auto-verifies, checkpoints, accepts locally, closes, and cleans up. Docs/config-only
diffs are detected automatically; admin/no-merge paths are routed by DB state.
Escape hatch: `ST_DIFF_GATE=off` for emergencies.

Subtasks: pass --citation or --none to record memory citations before close.
Already-completed task/subtask is a no-op (exit 0).

params.name: citation
params.help: Memory citation (subtask form): M:abc12345, G:abc12345, or 'Applied: [M:abc12345]'. Repeat for multiple.

params.name: paths
params.help: Only commit selected task paths; repeat for multiple paths. Preserves unrelated work.

params.name: acknowledge_none
params.help: Acknowledge no memories were needed (subtask form).

params.name: evidence
params.help: JSON with acceptance_receipt (requires --paths), deployment_receipt and/or source-bound live_validation checks.

routes.summary: Abandon a task or subtask and roll back tracked code changes.
routes.help:
Abandon a task or subtask and roll back tracked code changes.

For subtasks: Resets subtask status (single-pass).
For tasks: Two-pass confirmation required.

First run shows what will be destroyed and generates a confirm token.
Second run with --confirm TOKEN executes the abandon.

SAFE: Database is NOT restored. This uses append-only task metadata,
preventing data loss when other tasks were created after this task's
checkpoint was taken.

 
Examples:
  st abandon 1.1 -t task-abc123              # Reset subtask status
  st abandon task-abc123                     # Preview blast radius
  st abandon task-abc123 --confirm a1b2c3d4  # Execute with preview token

routes.summary: Log episode citations with suffix notation ratings.
routes.help:
Log episode citations with suffix notation ratings.

Citations use suffix notation for three-signal rating:
- M:abc12345+  -> mandate helpful (promotes episode)
- G:def67890-  -> guardrail harmful (demotes episode)
- M:xyz99999   -> used/neutral (no suffix)

Use --none ONLY if you have honestly reflected and determined that none of
the injected memories in <memory-context> were applicable to this subtask.
If ANY memory helped guide your approach, cite it instead.

If no task_id is provided, uses the active context from 'st work'.

Examples:
    st subtask citations M:abc12345+ G:def67890- --subtask 1.1
    st subtask citations M:85bf4635+ -s 2.1
    st subtask citations --none -s 1.1  # Only if truly no memories helped

routes.summary: Jujutsu workflow through st.
routes.help:
Jujutsu workflow through st.

Principles:
  - Use st vcs doctor/reconcile for cross-repo hygiene.
  - Agents call st jj or st commit, not raw jj.
  - All commands run with --no-pager and non-interactive editor config.

Common workflows:
  st jj status | init --repo /path | new -m "msg" | describe -m "msg"
  st commit -m "fix" --push --task task-abc
  st jj push --bookmark main --revision main
  st jj log --limit 20 | op-log --limit 20 | remote-bookmarks <name>
  st jj undo --task task-abc | op-restore <op-id> --task task-abc
  st jj conflicts | revert <rev> --message "rollback" --push --task task-abc

Usage: st db [-P PROJECT] count <TABLE>
Count rows in one table.

Usage: st db [-P PROJECT] ddl "CREATE INDEX ..."
Limited ad hoc DDL: CREATE INDEX or ALTER TABLE <table> ADD. Use migrations for versioned schema changes.

Usage: st db [-P PROJECT] exec "UPDATE ..."
Run write SQL; DROP, TRUNCATE, GRANT, REVOKE, and CREATE are blocked. Use migrations for schema changes.

Usage: st db [-P PROJECT] indexes [TABLE]
Show public-table indexes; omit TABLE for all.

Usage: st db [-P PROJECT] migrate <status|upgrade|downgrade|history|create|create-manual> [ARG]
status shows current revision; upgrade defaults to head; downgrade defaults to -1; history defaults to 10 revisions; create and create-manual require a message.

Usage: st db [-P PROJECT] migrate create "MESSAGE"
Create an autogenerated Alembic revision.

Usage: st db [-P PROJECT] migrate create-manual "MESSAGE"
Create an empty Alembic revision for manual edits.

Usage: st db [-P PROJECT] migrate downgrade [REVISION]
Revert migrations through REVISION; default is -1 (one revision).

Usage: st db [-P PROJECT] migrate history [COUNT]
Show recent Alembic history; default count is 10.

Usage: st db [-P PROJECT] migrate status
Show the current Alembic revision.

Usage: st db [-P PROJECT] migrate upgrade [REVISION]
Apply migrations through REVISION; default is head.

Usage: st db [-P PROJECT] query [-t|--plain] "SELECT ..."
Run one diagnostic SQL statement in a read-only transaction; -t/--plain emits unaligned rows.

Usage: st db [-P PROJECT] sample <TABLE> [LIMIT]
Show table rows; default limit is 10.

Usage: st db [-P PROJECT] schema <TABLE>
Show public-table columns, nullability, defaults, and indexes.

Usage: st db [-P PROJECT] sizes
Show public-table total and table sizes, largest first.

Usage: st db [-P PROJECT] tables [--counts]
List public tables; --counts also calculates row counts.

Usage: st db [-P PROJECT] workbench start|stop|status [--admin]
Start Pgweb read-only by default; --admin applies to start.

Usage: st db [-P PROJECT] workbench start [--admin]
Start Pgweb read-only by default; --admin allows writes.

Usage: st db [-P PROJECT] workbench status
Show Pgweb state and proxy URL when running.

Usage: st db [-P PROJECT] workbench stop
Stop the project Pgweb workbench.
